presentation: 35-year-old with sore throat, fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy.
history: Symptoms started 2 days ago after exposure at work.
exam: T 38.5C, pharyngeal erythema with exudate, no rash.

presentation: 28-year-old with burning chest pain after meals, worse when supine, relieved by antacids.
history: Symptoms started after a large meal. No fever, no cough.
imaging: Upper GI endoscopy shows distal esophageal erosions.

presentation: 3-year-old with barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarseness. Symptoms worse at night. No drooling.
history: No prior episodes.
exam: T 38.8C, mild subcostal retractions. No toxic appearance.
progression: Improved with dexamethasone and cool mist.

presentation: 65-year-old with painful eye, red eye, photophobia, fuzzy vision. History of glaucoma. Shallow anterior chamber.
history: Sudden onset while watching TV.
exam: IOP markedly elevated on tonometry. Corneal edema.

presentation: 50-year-old with progressive exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, bilateral lower-extremity edema over 3 weeks. History of poorly controlled hypertension.
history: Prior MI 2 years ago.
exam: Elevated JVP, S3 gallop, bibasilar crackles.
imaging: CXR shows pulmonary venous congestion and cardiomegaly; echo EF 35%.
progression: Improved with diuresis and GDMT titration.
mcq_options: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
final_diagnosis: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
differential_diagnoses: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

presentation: 22-year-old with right lower quadrant pain, nausea, anorexia for 24 hours. Last menstrual period 5 days ago.
history: No prior similar episodes.
exam: Fever 38.2C, RLQ rebound tenderness, positive Rovsing sign.
imaging: CT abdomen shows dilated appendix with peri-appendiceal fat stranding.

presentation: 40-year-old with recurrent abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, weight loss. Colonoscopy shows skip lesions and cobblestoning.
history: Brother also has IBD.
exam: Abdominal tenderness in RLQ and LLQ with mass-like thickening.
imaging: CT enterography shows small bowel strictures.

presentation: 30-year-old with facial rash across cheeks, photosensitivity, arthralgias, fatigue. ANA positive 1:640.
history: Symptoms wax and wane over months.
progression: Improved on hydroxychloroquine and low-dose prednisone.

presentation: 45-year-old with episodic headaches, visual auras, and sudden-onset severe occipital headache during exertion. Family history of similar headaches.
history: Episodes since adolescence but recently more frequent and severe.
exam: Blood pressure and neuro exam normal between episodes. During episode: nuchal rigidity not present.
labs: Labs normal. D-dimer elevated during episode but not between.
imaging: CT negative during resolved headache. CTA shows no aneurysm. MRV incomplete due to motion.

presentation: 60-year-old with stepwise cognitive decline, early urinary incontinence, and gait apraxia over 8 months.
history: History of hypertension and remote head trauma.
exam: Mini-mental score 22/30, gait wide-based with difficulty turning, frontal release signs bilaterally.
labs: B12, TSH, syphilis serology normal. CSF protein mildly elevated.
imaging: MRI shows leukoaraiosis and ventriculomegaly out of proportion to cortical atrophy.
progression: Slowly progressive; shunt trial under evaluation.

presentation: 55-year-old with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, hemoptysis, and cavitary lung nodules.
history: Former smoker, no prior autoimmune disease.
exam: Blood pressure 168/98, crackles at left upper zone.
imaging: CT chest shows cavitary nodules in both upper lobes; renal biopsy shows pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis.

presentation: 38-year-old with heat intolerance, weight loss, palpitations, goiter, exophthalmos. TSH suppressed.
history: Family history of thyroid disease.
exam: Tachycardia 118 bpm, fine tremor, warm moist skin, exophthalmos, thyroid bruit.
labs: Free T4 elevated, TSH receptor antibody positive.

history: Allergy season onset.

presentation: 70-year-old with recurrent falls, confusion, and urgency for 6 months. History of prior BPH.
history: Family reports shuffling gait and stooped posture.

presentation: 45-year-old with progressive dysphagia to solids and now liquids, regurgitation of undigested food, weight loss.
history: Symptoms progressive over 2 years.
exam: Boggy mucosa in lower esophagus on endoscopy.
imaging: Barium swallow shows dilated esophagus with retained food/debris and bird-beak narrowing.

presentation: 19-year-old with fever, candida esophagitis, chronic diarrhea, and recurrent sinopulmonary infections. On immunotherapy.
history: History of combined immunodeficiency in sibling.

presentation: 25-year-old with sudden-onset severe headache, nuchal rigidity, photophobia. No fever. Clear CSF xanthochromia.
history: Recent skiing trip with minor head trauma 3 days ago.
exam: Kernig and Brudzinski positive. No focal deficits.
progression: Improved after EVD placement; blood on CT 6 hours later.
